# J-Space

## Definition

J-Space is a proposed representation of an agent’s active judgments, affordances, uncertainties, values, tools, memories and interlocutors. It articulates the thrown landscape through which reasoning proceeds. At **#2** (How? / Word / Square C / Water; dynamis `−/+`; L2↔L3′), defined form acquires the capacity to move and transform. A formal J-Space must specify its variables, admitted alternatives, relations and observations before changes can be measured: which possibilities become near or remote, which contradictions remain live, which values govern selection, and how these relations reorganise with context. The represented field discloses selected relations within [[02-objective-internality|Objective Internality]]; the Life / World whole continues to contain the act by which it is represented.

## In the argument

The proposed [[39-s5-p2-j-space|judgment field]] makes the producing horizon available through its boundaries. **Circumscription without circumstance** occurs when a sharply bounded output conceals the source, permission, distribution or concern through which its boundary arose. Showing the admitted field together with those conditions lets a different circumstance challenge what previously appeared self-evident.

The Agentworld brief asks for a "narrow corridor: same decision-procedural grammar, sufficiently divergent world models" ([[symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief#Source PDF page 40|p. 40]]). Its scenario gives the proposed comparison a concrete pressure: participants must be intelligible to one another without their world-models collapsing into one. QL supplies a grammar of distinct related operations; MEF supplies situated lens, gauge and exclusion choices through which their models can be compared. This is an essay construction responsive to the brief’s demand. A measured implementation would need declared variables, transformations and returned observations.

A local evaluating agent can function as knower of a J-Space comparison, its model, memory, tools and comparison rules as means, and the admitted alternatives as known. Within a person’s containing inquiry, that whole comparison becomes a means. The [nested knowing relation](C41-Objective-Internality.md#2) retains both scopes within Life / Mind: inspecting a local centre makes it known through a further act, whose first-person condition has its own office.

The [[40-s5-p3-preference-hidden-zero|baseline of valuation]] and the [[41-s5-p4-bimba-energy-fields|Bimba reference relation]] expose what a difference is measured against. A reference can be locally present: a retained source, map, rule or earlier state may govern the current comparison as Bimba. The same reference is a situated Pratibimba relative to the wider sources and act which formed it. [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/bimba-pratibimba|Original and reflection]] therefore describe recursive offices. The current judgment field can contain and inspect a reference without declaring that reference self-grounding or claiming that every source lies outside the field.

Suppose two proposed route fields disagree. A common reference allows a comparison to locate different source dates, access conditions, exclusions or selection rules. A person’s returned gate report may then correct the reference map; a finding about inaccessible routes may require a changed rule or permission. Where the rule remains fitting, a corrected source can govern the next comparison under that retained rule. The finding reaches whichever condition and authority it identifies, and a later judgment inherits the dated evidence and warranted change. Drift, disagreement and correction now mean differences relative to a declared ground whose own producing conditions remain answerable. Their observability depends on this declared comparison and return, rather than an agent scoring itself against an unexplained baseline.

## Sources

[[02-objective-internality|Objective Internality]] (the mediating constitution whose selected relations the representation compares); circumscription without circumstance (the failure mode, absorbed above); [[40-s5-p3-preference-hidden-zero|Bradley-Terry Gauge Problem]] (the gauge whose hidden zero occupies the field's baseline); [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/bimba-pratibimba|Bimba-Pratibimba]] (the recursive original/reflection relation through which the Bimba Map anchors situated J-Spaces); [[symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief#Source PDF page 40|Agentworld Brief, p. 40]] (the decision-procedural-grammar demand J-space answers). Energy-based models, attractor landscapes, topological data analysis and graph dynamics are candidate formal tools. Each would require its particular state space, transformations and observations; naming one does not supply an executed measurement. The proposed [[41-s5-p4-bimba-energy-fields|reference-field construction]] keeps that research task explicit.
